selection_rationale: Candidate A is the strongest fit: it directly addresses the identified gap (G1) with a preregistered paired controlled-fault design that matches the rehearsal constraint of exactly 40 confirmatory paired tasks, received a "pass" verdict from critics, and has feasible supporting evidence. Its primary outcome is clear and falsifiable and the required repairs before preregistration are actionable.
unresolved_uncertainties: Simulator⇄verifier concordance: deterministic verifier passes may not fully reflect production safety without validated concordance testing.
Per-fault-class power and external validity: n=40 may limit inference on individual fault classes and vendor-feature diversity.
Harmful over-repair detection coverage: operational intent loss detection rules may miss subtle semantic harms.
Verifier-exploitation risk remains possible despite single-repair budget and needs monitoring during execution.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Enumerate and freeze the exact set of deterministic fault operators and per-vendor task templates; archive and hash the task-generation code and resulting task bank.
Pre-register and justify sample-size/power assumptions for the paired primary test (or report minimal detectable effect sizes given n=40).
Design and validate verifier↔simulator concordance on a disjoint validation set; specify how verifier/simulator disagreements will be handled in analysis.
Specify precise harmful-change detection rules and independent safety checks, freeze the repair prompt and failure-label schema, and commit to logging all diffs, timestamps, and low-level artifacts.
